text: Imagine a colleague who wakes up every morning with no memory of yesterday.
That is how Claude works: each conversation starts fresh, with no carry-over from earlier chats.
Short-term memory lives only in your current conversation.
Saved, or persistent memory, consists of notes stored for Claude to read at the start of future chats—such as project instructions or team conventions.
Memory is not Claude learning on its own; it is a notebook of saved notes that you control.
Store your role, guidelines, and formatting preferences.
Never store passwords, customer personal data, or confidential material.
Keep your notes tidy and updated.
